key_insight: Probe scores only become interpretable when compared against a floor and a ceiling; the meaningful signal is the headroom between what simple inputs already reveal and what the full input can predict.
engineering_relevance: For model debugging and deployment, this reframes interpretability probing as an information-gain test, helping engineers distinguish genuine latent computation from easy-to-read input cues.
method: Define a floor from a declared set of simple inputs and a ceiling from the full input.
Measure probe performance relative to both reference points to estimate headroom.
Apply the framework to synthetic transformers, scGPT, and four LLM probing case studies.
evidence_signal: On transformers for in-context meta-analysis, distribution shift caused probe scores to drop and prediction error to rise 12–15×, yet the model still recovered a similar fraction of headroom, suggesting the data—not the representation—lost information.
watch_item: Floor and ceiling choices are task- and dataset-dependent, so weakly specified reference inputs can make headroom estimates misleading.
paper_title: How High Is 0.6? Floors, Ceilings, and Headroom in Interpretability Probing
